explain.say: Young skin is smooth and springy because of a strong, stretchy support layer underneath. With age, that support slowly weakens, and the skin starts to fold into wrinkles.

faq.a: Collagen is the most common protein in the body. In skin, its strong fibres form a supporting mesh in the dermis that keeps skin firm and thick. The body makes less of it as we age.
asks: What does collagen do for skin?
Why does collagen decrease with age?

faq.a: Elastin is a stretchy protein that lets skin and other tissues spring back after being stretched. Over the years the fibres break down and are hardly replaced, so skin loses its bounce.
asks: Why does old skin not spring back?

faq.q: Why does sunlight make skin age faster?
faq.a: Ultraviolet light in sunlight damages collagen and elastin fibres in the dermis and triggers enzymes that break them down. Skin often exposed to the sun wrinkles sooner than skin usually covered.

faq.q: Why do wrinkles form around the eyes and mouth?
faq.a: Smiling, squinting and frowning fold the skin in the same places thousands of times. As skin loses its spring, those folds stop smoothing out and become lasting lines, such as crow's feet.

faq.q: Why do fingers wrinkle in the bath?
faq.a: Bath wrinkles are different from ageing wrinkles. Nerves trigger blood vessels in the fingertips to narrow when skin is soaked, and the skin puckers. It goes away once you dry off.
asks: Why do fingers go wrinkly in water?
Are bath wrinkles the same as old age wrinkles?

facts: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the human body.
Skin that is regularly exposed to sunlight shows signs of ageing earlier than skin that is usually covered.

quiz.say: Which stretchy protein lets young skin spring back after you pinch it?
quiz.why: Elastin fibres in the dermis stretch and recoil; as they wear out with age, skin springs back more slowly.
